THE AMERICAN PEOPLE ARE CLEAR: NO MORE U.S. AID TO ISRAEL Today, the U.S. House of Representatives will vote on an amendment introduced by Rep. Thomas Massie to cut the $3.3 billion in annual U.S. military aid to Israel. I strongly support this amendment. Israel, like any other country, had the right to defend itself against the horrific terrorist attack by Hamas on October 7, 2023, which killed 1,200 innocent people. But it did not have the right to go to war against the entire Palestinian population. It did not have the right to kill more than 73,000 Palestinians and wound over 173,000 more — the vast majority of them women, children and the elderly. It did not have the right to destroy virtually the entire infrastructure of Gaza — the schools, the health facilities, the water systems, wastewater plants, the electric grid that a civilian population depends on to survive. It did not have the right to destroy or damage 92% of all housing units in Gaza. In other words, Israel did not have the right to commit genocide. And it did not have the right to escalate its violence and annexation of the West Bank while the world's attention was focused elsewhere. Tragically, almost five months ago, Israel, with strong support from the Trump administration, launched a reckless and illegal war against Iran — a war that has killed thousands of people and left an already unstable region of the world even more unstable. That war expanded into Lebanon, where Israeli strikes have now killed more than 4,000 people and displaced some 20% of the entire Lebanese population. That is not "defending Israel". These are regional wars of expansion and terror, waged without a clear strategy, and without an end in sight. The American people are catching on. Polls show that nearly three-quarters of Democratic voters now oppose sending military aid to Israel, as do more than one-third of Republican voters. Just 16% of all Americans support giving Israel unconditional aid. And I am proud that this past April, 40 out of 47 Senate Democrats — a record number — supported my bill to block arms sales to the far-right, extremist Netanyahu government. We have enormous unmet needs in our own country. Today, while 60% of our people are living paycheck to paycheck, tens of millions of Americans cannot afford housing, healthcare, childcare and other basic needs. Congress must focus on the needs of their constituents, not an Israeli government that is undermining American values. I urge my colleagues in the House to vote yes on the Massie amendment.

C001035.text: In addition to calling on the DHS Inspector General to conduct an independent investigation of this week’s fatal shooting in Biddeford involving ICE personnel, @SenAngusKing and I are calling on the Department of Justice to coordinate with Maine state and local law enforcement throughout its investigation. The people of Maine deserve clear answers about the circumstances surrounding this shooting. Cooperation among federal, state, and local law enforcement is essential to providing those answers and giving the public greater confidence that the investigation is thorough, fair, and impartial.

Today, I joined my colleagues in the Maine delegation – @SenAngusKing, @chelliepingree, and @RepGolden – in calling for a comprehensive, transparent, and expedited investigation into the fatal shooting involving ICE personnel in Biddeford. We are also asking DHS to detail the extent to which it will collaborate with state and local agencies.

I spoke with DHS Secretary Mullin last night and urged him to cease all non-urgent vehicle stops in the wake of yesterday’s deadly Biddeford shooting. I am encouraged that the Department has agreed to do so. An impartial investigation into the shooting in Biddeford needs to proceed, as the details surrounding this tragedy are important. It is extremely unfortunate that the agent involved did not have a body-worn camera. In April, measures that I authored in the Homeland Security funding bill became law, including $20 million for expanded use of body-worn cameras, $2 million for de-escalation training, and a 17% increase in the independent Office of Inspector General’s budget to investigate matters such as this shooting. The Democratic government shutdown delayed enactment and implementation of these important safety measures. While it is clear ICE needs to improve its performance, it is important to remember that the work ICE does to protect our country goes far beyond immigration enforcement. ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) is tasked with combating cartels, human smuggling, child exploitation, forced labor, and more. Eliminating ICE would make our country less safe and endanger the lives and welfare of countless individuals.

While the investigation of the Biddeford shooting is not yet complete, it raises sufficient critical questions that I spoke with DHS Secretary Mullin last night and urged him to cease all non-urgent vehicle stops.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin has informed me that the Boston office of the DHS Inspector General has taken over the investigation of the Biddeford shooting in cooperation with the FBI.

Today, I stood alongside 23 Veterans Service Organizations and the surviving brother of Major Richard Star in support of the Taking Care of America's Veterans Act, which is expected to be considered on the House Floor later this week. This bipartisan legislation includes key provisions of my Major Richard Star Act, bringing long-overdue justice to nearly 60,000 medically retired combat Veterans by restoring concurrent receipt of the retirement pay and disability benefits they earned through their service and sacrifice. While I remain committed to achieving full concurrent receipt for every disabled Veteran, this package represents a significant step forward and will provide meaningful, immediate relief to tens of thousands of our nation's heroes. In addition to the Richard Star provisions, the bill includes 59 other bipartisan measures that will strengthen benefits and services for Veterans, surviving spouses, caregivers, and military families. The urgency of passing this legislation has never been greater. Earlier today, the Department of Veterans Affairs advanced its rulemaking process to implement proposed changes to future disability ratings for tinnitus and sleep apnea - the very policies that serve as the funding mechanism for this legislative package. If those changes are implemented administratively rather than through Congress, the resulting savings will be diverted elsewhere instead of being reinvested in critical Veteran priorities. Congress has a clear opportunity to ensure those savings are used to fulfill our promises to those who have worn the uniform. The time to act is now. Our Veterans—and the families who have sacrificed alongside them—have waited far too long.

B000490.text: This week, the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, appeared before the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government. During the hearing, I asked the Director about how Congress can be any clearer to ensure that the Trump Administration understands that once a funding bill is signed into law, the President is not allowed to change or second-guess the spending and withhold it due to policy or political differences. That is at the heart of Article 1 of the U.S. Constitution and why Congress also passed the Impoundment Control Act of 1974, when President Nixon tried to withhold funds that were already obligated according to the law.

This week, I asked the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, to explain how poorly planned cuts to the federal workforce last year have weakened services and protections upon which Americans rely. This includes the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, which is responsible for protecting America’s agriculture from invasive species and diseases. USDA-APHIS began mounting a vigorous response to the resurgence of New World Screwworm – a deadly parasite affecting livestock – in 2024. However, in early 2025, the Administration illegally fired workers and forced others to resign, causing over 25 percent of all USDA-APHIS employees to leave. USDA’s New World Screwworm prevention, monitoring, surveillance, and control efforts were halted. USDA had approved $378 million in prevention and control funding for sterile fly facilities in 2023 and 2024, yet the money went unspent when the new administration paused funding. This is extremely concerning to our ranchers, and this outbreak could drive the price of food even higher. Unfortunately, we continue to see the fallout of the blunt and ill-considered cuts to federal workers, from the return of New World Screwworm to the United States, to farmers showing up to closed or understaffed Farm Service Agency offices, to attacks on our nuclear safety programs putting national security at risk. I will continue to hold the White House accountable, as I did this week during the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government hearing with Mr. Vought.

There are few corners of Capitol Hill where South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham wasn't known. Whether you knew him personally or simply watched him at work, he was impossible to ignore.   Lindsey was a ubiquitous presence in Washington – with few office holders as visible, quotable, or energetic as him. For more than three decades, he served throughout the House and Senate – building a reputation as a determined legislator, a media presence, and a dealmaker. From the green rooms to the global stage, Lindsey was always in the middle of the debate, making the case for what he believed in for South Carolina and the nation.   When it came to foreign affairs, Graham was an old-fashioned statesman and hawk. He believed America was a force for good in the world, and he never hesitated to confront those who threatened our interests and our allies – from Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea to terrorist organizations around the globe.   As Appropriators serving in different chambers, we worked together and shared a commitment to a strong national defense. I always appreciated his insight, his candor, and his willingness to pick up the phone to exchange ideas, discuss Oklahoma figures or issues, or strategize how we could bridge differences between the House and Senate. He was never shy about calling to seek advice, compare notes, or test his own impressions – a quality that reflected both his confidence and his respect for the views of others.   Lindsey approached public service with boundless energy, sharp wit, and genuine optimism. He loved serving in Congress, and it showed every day. He was a gifted communicator, a persuasive advocate, and someone who never lost his enthusiasm for the institution or for the work of governing.   I will miss Senator Lindsey Graham, and so will the Congress he served so faithfully. His gregarious nature always left us with points made crispy, cleanly, and with a laugh. That energy and humor certainly made him the ‘happy warrior’ of his political generation. His leadership, collegiality, and unmistakable presence will be deeply missed.

Specifically: - In July 2025, I released, in coordination with then Director of National Intelligence Gabbard, the 2017 HPSCI Majority Staff report on the Russia Hoax, which showed the American people how individuals in the intelligence community manipulated and fabricated intelligence in a conspiracy against a President of the United States. - Then in June this year, following three years of my Committee investigation detailing the manipulation and concealment of intelligence by analysts on Anomalous Health Incidents (AHIs), former Director Gabbard recalled the Intelligence Community Assessments (ICAs) on AHIs, which involved similar corrupt acts. To be clear, there are great patriots working in the Intelligence Community who are dedicated to doing the right thing to uphold U.S. national security. But we learned tonight of some whose actions are an affront to the Constitution and rule of law. Their actions dishonor those serving their country honestly. I have seen far too many instances of intelligence bureaucrats who think they not only know better than the American people, but better than the Presidents the American people elect. This is unacceptable. Americans and their elected leaders must be able to trust the Intelligence Community and the intelligence they produce—it’s a Constitutional and national security imperative. To those politicians or talking heads who want the American people to ‘move on’ from 2020 and ‘stop looking back and look forward’—my response to you is we cannot go forward with an eroded, weak foundation. We must look ahead while also seeking to fully understand what went wrong and hold bad actors accountable. Telling the American people to just 'move on' is an arrogant and patronizing affront. Instead, tonight, President Trump trusted the American people with the facts, allowing them to arrive at their own conclusions. We, the American people, deserve that much. As a country, we are trying to move forward, but sometimes sunshine is the best disinfectant. Now it's time to hold people accountable, or this will keep happening. It’s not too late. I will continue working with President Trump and trusted members of his team to do just that.

For 250 years, our great experiment has faltered, flourished, evolved, and progressed. The American experience is ever-changing and as diverse as the people who call this country home. But one thing has remained constant – the idea of America has always been a beacon of hope. Protecting this country and the ideals and values it was founded on takes work. Democracy is demanding. It takes dedication and principle. And it takes the resounding belief that upholding those ideals and values is worth the fight because America is bigger than any one person. Because liberty can only truly endure when it is paired with responsibility, virtue, and a commitment to put public good ahead of personal ambition. Today, we celebrate the moment when our founding fathers openly declared that creating this country, based in liberty, was a necessity in the face of tyranny. Their legacy is that leadership requires courage when it’s difficult, integrity when no one is watching, and a willingness to put country above self. We must remember that our duty is not merely to the next election, but to the next generation. That should be the challenge for all Americans as we look forward to another 250 years. From Massachusetts, where the fight for freedom first began, I wish you a happy 4th of July. God Bless America always, God Bless all who call her home, and God Bless our courageous men and women in uniform who continue the fight for liberty today.

D000623.text: Today marks 82 years since the deadliest home front disaster of World War II – the Port Chicago munitions explosion in Concord. More than 300 men were killed that day and nearly 400 were injured, mostly African American servicemembers, who were working in unsafe conditions. Following this devastating disaster, hundreds of servicemembers at Port Chicago banded together, refusing to work under the unsafe conditions and requesting additional training – 50 of these men were charged with mutiny and dishonorably discharged. I, and my predecessor George Miller, collectively spent decades advocating in Washington, D.C. for these wrongful mutiny convictions to be erased, and we finally secured the exoneration of the Port Chicago 50 in 2024. Today is a solemn day, to remember the lives lost here in Contra Costa and the grievous wrong done to 50 men who did not live to see their convictions erased, but also a chance to see how we can right the wrongs of the past. To learn more about the Port Chicago 50, tune in to my earlier conversation with Reverend Diana McDaniel, Co-founder and President of the Friends of Port Chicago National Memorial: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QpQ20zU87ig&t=2s

F000466.text: Pearline Compton of Bristol Borough was the kind of woman every community hopes to have—someone whose faith, kindness, and quiet strength made every life she touched better. Born in Kelly, Louisiana, Pearline came to Bucks County as a young woman and built a life rooted in hard work, humility, family, and service. Over time, she became deeply woven into the fabric of our community. For more than 33 years, Pearline worked as a skilled press operator at Falls Manufacturing in Fairless Hills, and remarkably, never missed a single day of work. That tells you something about who she was. Dependable. Disciplined. Proud of honest work. Faithful in every responsibility placed before her. But Pearline’s greatest legacy was not only in the work she did. It was in the love she gave and the community she helped strengthen. In 1986, after the passing of her beloved niece, Eula Mae Hamilton, Pearline opened her heart and her home to Eula’s young daughters, Chrissandra and my dear friend, Valerie Hamilton, and raised them as her own. For those who know Chrissandra and Valerie, you know the remarkable women they became, and can see Pearline’s love, strength, and steady hand in both of them. That same heart extended far beyond her own home. Pearline poured herself into her community, supporting children, families, neighbors, and local organizations with the same devotion that defined her life. Through Children of God Educational Services, in Historic Bristol Borough, established and led by Valerie, she shared wisdom, encouragement, kindness, and love with young people and families across our community. That is what hometown heroes do. They show up. They love deeply. They serve quietly. They lift children, strengthen families, support neighbors, and leave a community better than they found it. Pearline Compton lived 94 years that way—with faith in action, love made visible, and kindness strong enough to shape generations. Please join me in extending heartfelt condolences to Chrissandra, Valerie, Pearline’s entire family, and all who were blessed to know and love her.

Today, I voted for an amendment to eliminate $3.3 billion in military assistance funding for Israel in this year's national security funding bill. I want to be clear about why.  The status quo is unsustainable. Prime Minister Netanyahu has used American military assistance funding to carry out atrocities in Gaza, embolden violent settlers in the West Bank, and continue indiscriminate bombing in Lebanon. He has shown us again and again that he does not respond to reason. He responds only to direct pressure.  It is not a break from what I believe. I have always affirmed Israel's right to exist as a Jewish state and its right to defend itself from attack. This vote doesn't change that. I also remain convinced that a path toward Palestinian self-determination is the only viable way to achieve a peaceful future in the region, and Netanyahu's government has spent years working to foreclose that path.  Because I know how this vote will be twisted by some, it’s important to be direct about something else. Criticism of Netanyahu's government is not criticism of the Jewish people. At a moment when antisemitism is rising in our country and around the world, that distinction matters. I have condemned antisemitism and religious hatred at every turn, and I always will. Anyone who uses this debate as cover for hate will find no ally in me.  The stakes here are bigger than one vote. Netanyahu is turning one of America's greatest allies into a pariah, one that has lost support from the international community. Netanyahu needs to change course. Until he does, the American people should not be asked to write a blank check.

I am voting Yes on the amendment to State Department appropriations to zero out $3.3 billion in foreign military financing for Israel. If enacted, this measure would prevent the U.S. government from financing and selling attack aircraft, bombs & missiles, and targeting systems to the Israel Defense Forces. It would not affect U.S. support for Israel’s Iron Dome, David’s Sling, or Arrow air-defense systems. The authority from Congress to finance and sell American-made weapons to allies is a grant of trust to both a presidential administration and its counterparty heads of government. With their disastrous war against Iran, their empowerment of settler violence in the West Bank, and their strategic incoherence against Islamist terrorism, both President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu have sacrificed that trust. Congress must act where the executives have failed. I acknowledge that this amendment is not the ideal mechanism of action. Its sponsor, Representative Thomas Massie, recently ran a re-election campaign that featured antisemitic tropes. Also, the State Department has not issued clear guidance about whether the amendment could affect humanitarian programming, embassy operations, or West Bank security assistance; if the amendment becomes law, I will work with colleagues to hold harmless those efforts. I have weighed these problems against the central thrust of the amendment: there must be consequences for Trump and Netanyahu. Those consequences should not impair the State of Israel’s right to defend itself against the atrocities of the terrorist regimes that threaten it. Israel and the United States have common interests, shared values, and a long history. Israel and the United States are allies. Before the next appropriations cycle in 2027, when this policy will again be up for debate, Israel will hold elections, the repercussions of the debacle in the Strait of Hormuz will become more clear, and negotiations between the United States and Israel over what replaces the Memorandum of Understanding will pick up pace. This presents an opportunity to renew the U.S.-Israel alliance on shared principles and a bipartisan basis.

RT by @RepRitchie: Everyone deserves clean air and a plan that works for them. If you or someone you care for has a disability or uses medical equipment, smoke emergencies take extra preparation, and NYCEM is here to help you get ready with guidance. Here's what to know. 💙 IF YOU USE ELECTRIC MEDICAL EQUIPMENT: Ventilators, oxygen concentrators, CPAP machines, and powered mobility devices all depend on electricity. Know your backup power options now, whether that's battery backup, a charged power bank, or a plan to relocate. Contact your utility to register as a life-sustaining equipment customer so you're prioritized during outages. IF YOU HAVE A RESPIRATORY OR HEART CONDITION: Smoke affects you sooner and more severely. Stay indoors with windows closed when air quality is poor, run AC on recirculate if available, and keep your medications, inhalers, and oxygen supplies stocked and within reach. Talk to your doctor now about what to do when air quality drops, including when to adjust activity or seek care. CREATE CLEANER AIR AT HOME: Designate one room with as few windows and doors as possible as your clean-air room. A HEPA portable air cleaner helps. Avoid candles, smoking, frying, and vacuuming, which add indoor pollution. BUILD YOUR SUPPORT NETWORK: Identify at least two people who can check on you during an emergency, help you get to cleaner air, or assist with an evacuation. Share your plan, your medication list, and how your equipment works. If you rely on a home health aide or paratransit, ask your providers about their emergency procedures. PACK A GO-KIT THAT FITS YOUR NEEDS: Medications and copies of prescriptions, backup batteries and chargers for medical and mobility equipment, hearing aid batteries, glasses, communication cards or devices, comfort items, and instructions for your care that someone else could follow. STAY INFORMED YOUR WAY: Sign up for @NotifyNYC to get emergency alerts in the format that works for you, including accessible formats. Check air quality before going outside and plan around it. D000230.text: Friday in the First For decades, Wayne Peel, a Williamston resident, spent his days caring for the minds and well-being of others in mental health and public service. Now, in his retirement, he has turned that same spirit of service toward caring for his home. As the President of the Martin County Historical Society, Wayne is on a mission to ensure that the stories of eastern North Carolina don’t fade away. He understands that history isn't just a collection of dusty records; it tells the story of a community. Whether he’s working to preserve a historic landmark, carefully digitizing archives to save them for the future, or hosting "Lunch and Learn" sessions that bring neighbors together, Wayne is bridging the gap between yesterday and tomorrow. Through his dedication, he is teaching us that when we honor the people and events that shaped our region, we gain a deeper appreciation for where we stand today. Wayne is proving that retirement isn't just about slowing down; it’s about choosing a new way to pour your heart and soul into the place you call home. #FridaySpotlight

Nature is unpredictable but repeated failures to reduce wildfire risk and properly manage forests is a policy choice that is now affecting Americans' health. In Congress, I have worked to establish strong bilateral ties with Canadian officials and over the coming days, I am going to be using those relationships to discuss the importance of implementing better practices. Action is needed, now.

Americans should not be forced to breathe hazardous air year after year because Canada refuses to properly manage its forests. This is no longer a one-time emergency—it’s becoming an annual public health crisis. That is unacceptable. I am reaching out to Members of Parliament and the Canadian Ambassador to demand answers about the devastating impact Canada’s forest management failures are having on Western New York, the Southern Tier, and communities across the United States. Millions of Americans are paying the price for policies they had no role in creating. We can all accept that nature is unpredictable. But repeated failures to reduce wildfire risk and manage forests responsibly are a policy choice. The United States cannot continue accepting dangerous air quality every summer as the new normal. Canada must take meaningful action to prevent these catastrophic wildfires and protect both Canadians and Americans. If it refuses to do so, there should be consequences. Our citizens should not be forced to suffer because another nation’s government failed to do its job.

H001100.text: As Chairman of the House Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs, I recently chaired a hearing on the Missing and Murdered Indigenous People crisis. One point came through clearly: in many cases, the technology to solve these cases already exists. The challenge is making sure it’s actually used. Witnesses described how advanced DNA analysis and AI are helping solve cold cases and identify remains that once had no leads. Families who have waited years for answers deserve every available tool in the pursuit of justice. I’ll keep working to remove the barriers that stand in the way. #CO03

New satellite technology can now detect wildfires within minutes—day or night—giving firefighters valuable time before a small fire becomes a major one. I recently met with the team at OroraTech USA, a Colorado company using a network of 19 thermal satellites dedicated to wildfire detection. They’re already partnering with the City of Aspen, showing how Colorado innovation is helping strengthen wildfire response. In a district as large and wildfire-prone as #CO03, every minute matters. Better information means faster decisions, quicker response, and a better chance of stopping small fires before they become devastating ones.

Today I spoke on the House floor to recognize the service of the Beulah Volunteer Fire Department during the Aspen Acres Fire in Pueblo County. Several firefighters lost their own homes, yet they remained on the line protecting their neighbors. Their story speaks for itself. #CO03

Inspired by Independence Pass, Elizabeth’s artwork will be displayed in the Capitol for the next year alongside winning entries from across the country. It was a pleasure to welcome Elizabeth and her family to Washington to see her work on display. Congratulations, Elizabeth, on an outstanding accomplishment. I hope your success inspires more young artists across #CO03 to enter next year’s competition.

J000311.text: Today, we mourn the passing of United States Senator Lindsey Graham, a fierce advocate for the people of South Carolina.  May his memory be a blessing to his family and friends. Born in Upstate South Carolina, tragedy struck Lindsey early in his life.  After he graduated from high school, Lindsey’s mother and father passed away within 15 months of each other, leaving him without parents and his 13-year-old sister orphaned.  Lindsey shifted his focus to raising and caring for his sister, assuming a responsibility few can imagine at that age. The resilience and sense of duty he developed during those difficult years would come to define a lifetime of service. For 33 years, Lindsey served our Country in the United States Air Force.  He was awarded the Bronze Star for meritorious service shortly before retiring as a Colonel. For 31 years, Lindsey served in the United States Congress, and became one of the most influential lawmakers in our Country. Lindsey’s unexpected passing also affirms a profound truth: every day we live is a gift and a blessing from God.

A historic new frontier for India’s space journey! At 11:30 AM today, Skyroot Aerospace will undertake the maiden orbital launch of Vikram-1, India’s first privately developed launch vehicle. This four-stage rocket is designed to provide rapid and on-demand launch services. This mission highlights the talent, determination and entrepreneurial spirit of our youth. It also shows how our space-sector reforms are unlocking new opportunities for innovation and enterprise. My best wishes to the entire Skyroot Aerospace team for a successful launch. May Vikram-1 soar high, create history and inspire a generation of innovators. I urge all Indians, especially my young friends, to follow this historic mission and join in wishing Team Skyroot success using #IndiaWithVikram1. @SkyrootA
ਜਲੰਧਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੰਤ ਨਿਰੰਜਨ ਦਾਸ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਲਣ ਦਾ ਸੁਭਾਗ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਹੋਇਆ। ਅਧਿਆਤਮਿਕ ਜਾਗਰੂਕਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਮਾਜ ਭਲਾਈ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਯੋਗਦਾਨ ਬਹੁਤ ਹੀ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਨਾਦਾਇਕ ਹੈ।

R to @narendramodi: ਪੰਜਾਬ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਫ਼-ਸੁਥਰੇ, ਇਮਾਨਦਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਕਾਸ-ਮੁਖੀ ਸ਼ਾਸਨ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੈ। ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਭਾਜਪਾ ਦੀ ਡਬਲ-ਇੰਜਣ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਹੀ ਨਵਾਂ ਨਿਵੇਸ਼ ਲਿਆ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ, ਰੁਜ਼ਗਾਰ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ, ਕਿਸਾਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਸ਼ਕਤ ਬਣਾ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ, ਔਰਤਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਸ਼ਕਤ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਹ ਯਕੀਨੀ ਬਣਾ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਣੇ ਉਤਪਾਦ ਦੁਨੀਆ ਭਰ ਦੇ ਬਾਜ਼ਾਰਾਂ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਣ।

R to @narendramodi: ਪੰਜਾਬ ਕੋਲ ਬੇਮਿਸਾਲ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੋਂ ਦੇ ਮਿਹਨਤੀ ਕਿਸਾਨ, ਹੁਨਰਮੰਦ ਨੌਜਵਾਨ, ਉੱਦਮੀ ਸੋਚ ਅਤੇ ਖੇਡਾਂ ਦਾ ਗੁਣ ਸੂਬੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਵੀਆਂ ਬੁਲੰਦੀਆਂ 'ਤੇ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ। ਦੁੱਖ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਮੌਜੂਦਾ ਸੂਬਾ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਨੇ ਵਿਗੜਦੀ ਅਮਨ-ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ, ਨਸ਼ਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਖ਼ਤਰੇ, ਭ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟਾਚਾਰ, ਵਧਦੇ ਕਰਜ਼ੇ ਅਤੇ ਅਧੂਰੇ ਵਾਅਦਿਆਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਇਸ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਨਾਲ ਧੋਖਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ।

WORLD_FRANCE_PRESIDENT.text: La coopération entre l’Allemagne et la France est la condition nécessaire pour avancer en Europe.

En Allemagne, le Conseil des ministres franco-allemand que nous co-présidons aujourd’hui avec le Chancelier Friedrich Merz doit nous permettre de renforcer notre compétitivité, notre sécurité et notre défense et la résilience de nos démocraties. Le réflexe franco-allemand est plus que jamais nécessaire pour mettre en œuvre notre agenda de souveraineté, au service de nos peuples et notre Europe.

Le constat en 2017 était sans appel : quinze ans sans nouveau Canadair, dix ans sans nouveau Dash, une flotte aérienne vieillissante et une chaîne de production à l’arrêt. Depuis 2017, nous avons changé d’échelle en investissant plus d’1,5 milliard d’euros pour renforcer les moyens de la sécurité civile. Dès 2017, plus de 400 millions d’euros ont permis l’acquisition de six Dash 8 MRBET pour remplacer les anciens Tracker et renforcer la lutte contre les feux de forêt. À partir de 2022, plus d’un milliard d’euros supplémentaire a été engagé pour renouveler la flotte d’hélicoptères, acquérir de nouveaux Canadair, renforcer les moyens aériens et financer plus de 1000 camions-citernes supplémentaires. Jamais la Nation n’avait autant investi dans la sécurité civile. Cet effort se poursuivra.
